Move "nice-to-have" scripts to sandbox

This commit moves `conformal_map_taylor_coefficients.jl` and
`complex_jacobi_ellptic.jl` from main package to `sandbox`, allowing us to
remove most dependencies of `CubedSphere.jl`. `sandbox` now contains a Julia
environment with the packages needed to execute scripts in the folder.

Technically, this is a breaking change, so I bumped to 0.3.0.

No changes to the documentation seem to be required.

Conformally map an irregularly spaced grid on the reference square to a more uniform grid on the cubed sphere panel (#41)

* Enlarged corner cells with near-orthogonality

Added the script 'elliptic_quasi_conformal_cubed_sphere_grid.jl' in the 'src'
directory, which leverages elliptic grid generation techniques to enlarge corner
cells of the conformal cubed sphere while preserving near-orthogonality. This
potentially offers a solution to both computational intensity and grid alignment
concerns.

* Optimized cubed sphere grid using EKI

Refined the quasi-conformal cubed sphere grid using the Ensemble Kalman
Inversion (EKI) method. EKI, an advanced derivative-free data assimilation
technique, iteratively adjusts model parameters to optimize performance and
accuracy, based on the comparison of model outputs with observational data. In
our application, EKI is employed to optimize the parameters of elliptic grid
generation, aiming to enhance the grid's quality. This improvement is measured
by steering three key grid diagnostics---orthogonality, isotropy, and uniformity
of cell sizes---towards their ideal values representing the “observational data”
in our optimization process.

Compute spherical areas with StaticArrays instead of heap vectors (#56)

* Compute spherical areas with StaticArrays instead of heap vectors

`spherical_area_triangle` collected its vertices into `Vector`s and
used `LinearAlgebra.dot` and `cross` on them, i.e. BLAS, and
`spherical_quadrilateral_vertices` built its vertices as `Vector`s too.
Every area allocated, and the functions couldn't be used in GPU kernels
(Oceananigans computes the areas of tripolar grid cells in a kernel,
which with KernelAbstractions 0.10 is compiled even on the CPU, and the
BLAS call made LLVM abort).

Convert the vertices to `SVector`s instead of collecting them, which
accepts the same inputs (tuples, vectors) without allocating, and build
the vertices of `spherical_quadrilateral_vertices` as `SVector`s. The
areas don't allocate any more, and `compute_cell_areas` on a 40×40 grid
takes 144 μs and allocates 12.9 KB (its result) instead of 892 μs and
5.6 MB, with areas equal to the previous ones within 3e-15 relative.

* Specialize the allocation test helper on the function and its arguments

The allocation tests measured each call through a helper forwarding its
arguments as varargs, `allocations(f, args...)`. On Julia v1.10 and
v1.11 that method isn't specialized on the function it forwards to, so
the result of the measured call is boxed: the tests reported 16 bytes
for the areas (a boxed `Float64`) and 112 bytes for
`spherical_quadrilateral_vertices` (a boxed tuple of four `SVector`s),
although the functions themselves don't allocate.

Force the specialization with type parameters for the function and the
number of arguments, `allocations(f::F, args::Vararg{Any, N})`, which
measures zero bytes on Julia v1.10 to v1.13. Constraining only the
number of arguments isn't enough: it still allocates on v1.10 and v1.11.
